 Edited by Smriti Jain / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 19, 2026, 14:59 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Gold futures edged down by Rs 44 to Rs 1,29,770 per 10 grams on Thursday Gold prices have been tanking in the last few weeks, going way below their lifetime highs seen at the start of this year. From Rs 1.81 lakh per 10 grams to Rs 1.29 lakh - that’s a fall of almost 29%. Gold futures edged down by Rs 44 to Rs 1,29,770 per 10 grams on Thursday, as demand in the spot market remained subdued. On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold contracts for December delivery slipped Rs 44, or 0.03%, to Rs 1,29,770 per 10 grams. The contracts recorded a trading volume of 12,735 lots. Analysts attributed the marginal fall in gold prices to weak spot demand. In international markets, gold futures were largely unchanged at $3,739.85 per ounce in New York. Why is gold falling?
 So why is gold falling off the cliff suddenly? We ask experts: Gold’s initial decline followed profit-booking by investors after prices had risen to high levels, setting off a steep correction. Before the metal could stabilise, the US-Iran war erupted, sending crude oil prices past $120 per barrel and heightening fears of rising inflation. More recently, an unusually sharp surge in real yields has added to the pressure on gold prices, prompting further selling. The US Federal Reserve has increased interest rates for the first time since 2023. As inflation continues to remain high, expectations that the central bank could raise rates again in the coming months have gained strength. According to commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma, gold gave breakout below the previous consolidation range for the first time since September 2025 breaching the critical $3,800/Oz levels in Spot as strengthening bets on aggressive Fed tightening, amid rising inflationary concerns, strong consumer spending and hawkish central bank rhetoric, continued to fuel strength in dollar. What needs to be understood is that gold is a non interest yielding asset and when the US central bank hikes rates, bomd yields rise, shifting investor money to them. “The Dollar Index stands at its highest level in over 18 months against its major rivals, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury bond yields held firm around 5.10%,” he tells TOI. “Expectations of further Fed tightening in the coming months remains a headwind for gold in near term while gold is expected to remain volatile, with the direction of US yields and dollar index likely to remain the key drivers,” he adds. Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities says gold has witnessed significant profit booking in November month from Rs 1,450,00 to Rs 1,290,00 as market participants increasingly priced in the possibility of a US rate hike in December. Elevated inflation concerns and stronger demand for the dollar as a safe-haven asset have weighed on bullion. “Higher living and consumer spending costs could also limit investment demand for precious metals,” he tells TOI. Netra Deshpande, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan explains that precious metals are trading under pressure in the Indian markets tracking the global sell-off, dollar rise and underlying bullions falling sharply in the international markets on rising expectations of a Fed rate hike in December. “Domestic sentiment is also hurt by expectations that the RBI may raise rates at its December MPC meeting,” she tells TOI. “A sell-off in AI-related stocks has also added some liquidation in the counter to cover losses, but central bank gold purchases reached 321t in Q3, giving some support to the prices. Total SPDR gold ETF holdings are still up 2% this year at 100.9 million oz. Global geopolitical uncertainties also add to the safe haven bid,” she adds. Silver is falling sharply as tightening policies and slower growth weaken industrial demand. Where is gold headed?
 Analysts have mixed views on the near-term and long-term outlook for gold and silver. According to Maneesh Sharma, the 21-week EMA trading at around $3965/Oz is likely to remain a key upside barrier for Spot gold (CMP 3772/Oz). With no nearby moving-average-based supports on the chart, the metal remains vulnerable to further downside up to $3670 – 3640/Oz zone in near term basis in spot. “With gold yet to witness a new low for year 2026 it is still expected to outperform Silver in near term,” Sharma says “Meanwhile, the current fall in prices of gold has also delayed the expectation of a meaningful recovery in the first half of 2027, a 10–15 % recovery above $4500/Oz still looks possible in the second half of 2027 considering continued central-bank purchase & broader ETF inflows would strengthen support,” he adds. Jateen Trivedi cautions that with the Dollar Index hovering near 103.50, the near-term outlook for gold remains weak. “COMEX Gold needs to reclaim $4,000 to improve sentiment, while sustained trading below this level could keep downside pressure intact, with major support seen near 3,550–3,500,” he says.  “For a longer term perspective Rs 1,100,00 remains the support and 1,450,00 as a major resistance now,” Trivedi cautions. According to Netra Deshpande, the major immediate support for gold is around Rs 1,310,00 per 10 gram and for silver around Rs 1,630,00 per kg on MCX. “Overall, gold and silver are likely to trade in the steady to lower but wedding and festive jewellery demand and central bank buying will cap to the further sharp downside. Overall bullish bias in the long run is still intact in the domestic market,” she believes.
